fi-amphiprion-ocellaris.title: Ocellaris Clownfish (all designer morphs)
fi-amphiprion-ocellaris.summary: The classic 'Nemo' clownfish. Hardy, captive-bred and reef-safe. Every designer morph has the same care.
rows: About 4 in (11 cm max). Sold at about 1.25–1.5 in
15 gal or larger for one fish or a pair
Peaceful to semi-aggressive. Don't mix with other clownfish species
Keep one or a bonded pair. The larger fish becomes the female
Yes. Without an anemone it may host in a coral, which can irritate that coral
Frozen mysis or other marine frozen foods plus pellets, including some algae-based food. Feed 1–3 small meals a day
Indo-West Pacific reefs. These are captive-bred
notes: An anemone is optional. Bubble tip anemones are the usual host if you want one, but research their needs first.
Long-finned morphs do best in low to moderate flow.

fi-amphiprion-melanopus.title: Cinnamon Clownfish (tank raised)
fi-amphiprion-melanopus.summary: A red-and-black clownfish from the Coral Sea region. Captive-bred fish like this SKU are hardy and adapt well to aquarium life.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 12 cm (4.7 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one or a bonded pair; the larger fish becomes the female
Omnivore. Meaty frozen foods plus herbivore preparations
Pacific Ocean: Eastern Indonesia (Bali and Sulawesi eastward), south-eastern Philippines, Papua New Guinea, eastern Queensland, Coral Sea, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu. This SKU is tank raised
notes: Juveniles have thin white head bars that fade as they grow.

fi-amphiprion-perideraion.title: Pink Skunk Clownfish
fi-amphiprion-perideraion.summary: A pinkish clownfish with a white stripe along the back and another white bar just behind the eyes.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one or a pair; the larger fish is the female
Omnivore. Meaty foods plus herbivore preparations
Western Pacific: Gulf of Thailand and Cocos-Keeling in the eastern Indian Ocean to Samoa and Tonga, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
